observe.intro.title: Tap when you spot one
observe.intro.body: Every time you see a tiny creature nearby, tap its card. It helps us understand the health of this place.
observe.intro.tip.Bees: Fuzzy body, visiting flowers — good sign.
observe.intro.tip.Butterflies: Big wings, slow flutter. Moths count too.
observe.intro.tip.Flies: Big eyes, one pair of wings. Easy to mix up with bees — either guess is fine.
observe.intro.tip.Ants: On the ground, often in a line.
observe.intro.tip.Wasps: Slim waist, smoother than a bee.
observe.intro.tip.Spiders: Eight legs, no wings. Not an insect, but we still want it.
observe.intro.tip.Other: Anything else tiny and moving — tap it anyway.
observe.intro.tip.Bugs: True bugs — shield bugs, aphids, pointed mouthparts for piercing.
observe.intro.tip.Grasshoppers: Big back legs for jumping, often chirping in grass.
observe.intro.tip.Dragonflies: Long thin body, four wings held out flat, usually near water.
observe.intro.tip.Caterpillars: Long soft body, many legs. Any grub or larva counts too.
